test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Sept, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the bad.

options.text: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the worst.
Earlier, he was feeling good, but things took a turn for the bad.
Earlier, he was feeling well, but things took a turn for the ill.
Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the ill.

solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**took a turn for the bad**" is incorrect and not idiomatic.
 
• The correct idiomatic expression is "**took a turn for the worst**," which means that things got significantly worse.
 
• The word "**worst**" is the superlative form of "**bad**," which is appropriate to indicate the extreme negative change.
 
• The rest of the sentence "**Earlier, he was feeling better**" is correct and does not need any changes.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the worst.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2**: "Earlier, he was feeling good, but things took a turn for the bad." - This option is incorrect because "feeling good" is less appropriate than "feeling better," and "turn for the bad" is still incorrect.
 
• **Option 3**: "Earlier, he was feeling well, but things took a turn for the ill." - This option is incorrect because "took a turn for the ill" is not idiomatic, and "feeling well" is less precise in this context than "feeling better."
 
• **Option 4**: "Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the ill." - This option is incorrect because "took a turn for the ill" is not a correct idiomatic expression.
